questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Eritrea?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Tigrean” part of the Eritrea article.

questions.proof: The predominantly Tigrinya populated urban centers in Eritrea are the capital Asmara, Mendefera, Dekemhare, Adi Keyh, Adi Quala and Senafe, while there is a significant population of Tigrinya in other cities including Keren, and Massawa.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Eritrea?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Eritrea on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Eritrea article.

questions.proof: Eritrea has borders with the countries of Sudan, Ethiopia, and Djibouti.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Eritrea?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Tigrean” part of the Eritrea article.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Eritrea?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Eritrea article.

questions.proof: The currency of Eritrea is called the Nakfa.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Eritrean national identity began to develop during the Scramble for Africa, when _____ claimed Eritrea as one of its colonies.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “claimed”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Eritreans” part of the Eritrea article.

questions.proof: The Eritrean national identity began to develop during the Scramble for Africa, when Italy claimed Eritrea as one of its colonies.
